name: 1605 S. Prairie Avenue — the Illinois Central's 16th Street station (district draft; refined by T-1866)

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 2.000, v -6.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.609 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1605 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1605 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading '2-storey frame (yellow) building lettered ILLINOIS CENTRAL R.R. 16TH ST. STATION': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: frame.

parts.from: s20fp-1605-b1 p1 (main, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 98% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s20fp-1605-b1 p1 (main, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 98% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: Not a house: the sheet letters the two-storey frame building 'ILLINOIS CENTRAL R.R. 16TH ST. STATION' and Robinson 1886 shows a station on the same ground, so the census carries the use to 1904. It stands as the draft's two-storey gabled frame building with its own name and use, dressed as a station by T-2399: a timber platform on the track side, a canopy over it, a passenger door under a hood on the street and lettered nameboards. (The register's '1603' row is this frontage; the sheet prints 1605.) Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1355794894 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335. The station's dressing is RECONSTRUCTED (T-2399, liberty L-ic-16th-street-station-2399): neither sheet 20 nor Robinson 1886 draws a platform, a canopy, a door or a board, and no picture of this building is known (the Tribune's 1886 'Sixteenth Street Station' sketch is a one-storey depot that the library reads as the C. B. & Q. depot moved away, so it is not built toward). Only the platform's EDGE is read off the sheet: the nearest track's west rail, traced on sheet 20 through the T-1250 fit at 2.05 m off the track wall at the north end and 5.49 m at the south, less 1.0 m of clearance, so the platform tapers from 1.05 m to 4.5 m as the tracks bear away; the canopy stands only where the platform is deeper than it. The wording is the sheet's own lettering of the building, set as a railway's boards.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey frame (yellow) building lettered ILLINOIS CENTRAL R.R. 16TH ST. STATION'. Robinson 1886 shows a frame building lettered 16TH ST. STATION, I.C.R.R. here, so the station use is carried to 1904. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2335, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1866 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 20 trace (s20fp-1605-b1), the T-1840 census (s20-1605-f) and the T-1837 register row frontage-20-023; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335).
